did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jehoram son of Ahab ruled over Israel in Samaria for twelve years, beginning his reign in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
Did you know? Jehoram did evil in the eyes of the Lord, but unlike his father and mother, he removed the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had made.
Did you know? Although Jehoram removed the sacred pillar of Baal, he continued in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat—that is, the worship of the golden calves that Jeroboam had introduced.
Did you know? Mesha king of Moab is described as a sheep breeder, and he used to provide the king of Israel with one hundred thousand lambs and the wool of one hundred thousand rams.
Did you know? Jehoram asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah to join him in the war against Moab, and the king of Edom also joined the campaign.
Did you know? The three kings—of Israel, Judah, and Edom—chose to travel by way of the wilderness of Edom, but after seven days there was no water left for the army or the animals.
Did you know? Jehoshaphat asked for a prophet of the Lord, and Elisha was brought to him. Elisha is described as the one who poured water on Elijah’s hands.
Did you know? Before the prophecy about the water was given, Elisha asked for a musician to be brought. While the musician played, the hand of the Lord came upon Elisha.
Did you know? Elisha promised that the valley would be filled with water, even though the army would see neither wind nor rain, and that the water would be enough for both the people and the animals.
Did you know? The Moabites saw the water looking red in the sunlight, mistakenly interpreted it as blood, and assumed that the kings had killed one another. So they went out to take the spoil.
